tell: A black Google car, visible as dark bodywork at the bottom of the frame.
detail: Most Street View cars are white or silver, so a black car is a strong regional narrowing tool. The black-car group is concentrated in a handful of African coverages; use language and road markings to pick between them.

tell: Dust-caked white car with a prominent roof rack, on unpaved steppe tracks.
detail: Mongolian coverage is heavily off-road, so the car is filthy and the roof rack is unusually visible. The blur pattern around the rack is consistent enough to be a tell on its own.

tell: Low-mounted snorkel camera, often on a small hatchback, with visibly softer image quality.
detail: Much of India was shot with a lower-resolution rig mounted lower than usual, so the horizon sits differently and detail is mushy. Combine with Devanagari script and left-hand traffic.

tell: Long thin antenna rising from the car, visible against the sky.
detail: Sri Lankan coverage frequently shows a tall whip antenna. Together with left-hand traffic, Sinhala script and lush tropical vegetation it is a quick lock.

tell: Dirty light-coloured car with heavy dust streaks, on high-altitude roads.
detail: The Andean coverages share a grubby car look from unpaved mountain roads. Altitude vegetation, adobe buildings and the specific Spanish signage separate the three.

tell: No car visible at all, or only a small clean blur strip at the bottom.
detail: The best-maintained coverages hide the vehicle almost entirely. Absence of a car is itself information: it points away from Africa, Central Asia and South America and towards high-budget coverage.
